claims.text: Multi-principal-element mixing produces intrinsic lattice distortion in polycrystalline refractory HEAs.
Refractory HEAs tend to form secondary phases or precipitates during high-temperature exposure.
A minor alloying addition or tailored heat treatment can suppress secondary-phase evolution while maintaining the same refractory-HEA composition.
The proposed variants can be made to differ primarily in intrinsic lattice distortion while otherwise retaining equivalent composition and microstructure.
Suppressing secondary-phase formation lowers the effective contribution of lattice distortion in the BCC matrix.
Lattice distortion alters the local atomic energy landscape.
Enhanced lattice distortion raises high-temperature yield strength.
Enhanced lattice distortion reduces the rate of thermoelastic softening with temperature.
Lattice distortion delays the onset of high-temperature phase transformation.
Lattice distortion impedes grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Intrinsic lattice distortion primarily governs high-temperature mechanical and thermoelastic behavior, largely independently of secondary-phase evolution.
At 0.5–0.7 Tm, the variant with greater intrinsic lattice distortion will have higher yield strength than the phase-suppressed baseline.
At 0.5–0.7 Tm, the variant with greater intrinsic lattice distortion will show slower thermoelastic softening than the phase-suppressed baseline.
The comparison will isolate lattice-distortion effects from secondary-phase effects.

contradictions.description: A minor alloying-element addition necessarily changes composition, contradicting the statements that the modified baseline maintains identical or unchanged nominal composition.

The hypothesis describes lattice-distortion effects as largely independent of secondary-phase evolution, but the baseline assumes that suppressing secondary phases itself reduces the effective lattice-distortion contribution.
The proposed comparison changes both secondary-phase evolution and the asserted lattice-distortion mediator, so it does not isolate lattice distortion from secondary-phase effects as claimed.
